name: html-api
purpose: Parse and modify HTML correctly in PHP without a DOM. Two layers: a streaming tag-level editor and a full HTML5-spec-compliant tree-construction parser.

name: hooks-plugin-api
purpose: The extension mechanism the entire system is built on. Provides the action and filter engine through which 565 actions and 1638 filters are dispatched, plus plugin lifecycle registration.

name: style-engine
purpose: Convert style objects into CSS rules. A small, focused module that both block supports and global styles depend on.

name: cache-and-object-cache
purpose: A request-scoped in-memory cache designed to be transparently replaced by a persistent one via the object-cache.php drop-in. The default implementation does not persist across requests.

name: formatting-and-sanitization
purpose: Text transformation on the way in and out: escaping, sanitizing, typographic transformation and slashing. At 350 KB, formatting.php is the single largest file in WordPress.

name: database-wpdb
purpose: The entire data access layer. A single ~4230-line class with no ORM, no query builder and no server-side prepared statements. Every module reaches the database through the global $wpdb.

name: bootstrap-and-load
purpose: Turn a bare PHP request into a fully initialized WordPress runtime: locate configuration, verify host requirements, define constants, connect the database, start the object cache, load plugins and the theme, hand off to the request handler.

name: options-and-transients
purpose: WordPress's key-value store. Site configuration, plugin settings, cached remote data and expiring values all live in wp_options addressed by name. Read on every request via wp_load_alloptions(), making its caching behavior the largest single lever on WordPress performance.

name: kses-security
purpose: KSES Strips Evil Scripts: an HTML allowlist filter and the last line of defense for untrusted markup.

name: metadata
purpose: The generic attribute system. One implementation serves posts, comments, terms, users and blogs, driven by a $meta_type string that resolves to a table name.

name: error-handling-and-recovery-mode
purpose: Survive a fatal PHP error: catch it, identify which plugin or theme caused it, pause that extension, and email the administrator a link to a mode where the site loads without it.

name: posts-and-post-types
purpose: The central content entity. wp_posts stores posts, pages, attachments, revisions, nav menu items, reusable blocks, templates, global styles and fonts: 16 built-in types in one table distinguished only by the post_type column.

name: media-and-attachments
purpose: Upload handling, image resizing, responsive image markup and media metadata. The largest body of pure algorithmic code in WordPress: geometry, aspect-ratio matching and srcset generation.

name: users-roles-capabilities
purpose: The authorization model. Roles are named bundles of capabilities, capabilities are booleans, and a meta-capability layer translates object-specific questions into concrete capability checks. This is WordPress's entire access control.

name: taxonomy-and-terms
purpose: Classify objects via a three-table design (wp_terms, wp_term_taxonomy, wp_term_relationships) that separates the word from the classification from the assignment. The most normalized part of the WordPress schema and the source of its most confusing API.

name: comments
purpose: Accept, moderate and display reader responses plus trackbacks and pingbacks. The moderation pipeline is the most rule-dense business logic in WordPress core: a spam filter expressed as option-driven sequential checks.

name: query-and-loop
purpose: Turn a URL into a set of posts. WP parses the request into query variables, WP_Query compiles those into SQL, and The Loop iterates the result. WordPress's front controller, router and query layer combined.

name: authentication-and-sessions
purpose: Prove identity and maintain it across requests: password hashing, cookie-based sessions, session tokens, nonces, and the pluggable-function override mechanism.

name: blocks-library
purpose: The 115 built-in blocks. Each is a block.json plus, for dynamic blocks, a PHP render callback.

name: customizer
purpose: Live-preview theme and site settings with a changeset that can be saved, scheduled or discarded. Superseded by the Site Editor for block themes but still the settings surface for classic themes.

name: themes-and-templates
purpose: Choose which PHP or HTML file renders the current query, and manage theme registration, parent/child inheritance and theme features.

name: widgets-and-nav-menus
purpose: Two legacy content-placement systems that predate blocks and remain load-bearing: sidebar widgets and navigation menus.

name: block-editor
purpose: Parse, register and render the block-based content format. Post content is HTML with block boundaries encoded as HTML comments; this module turns that string into a tree and back.

name: script-modules-and-assets
purpose: Register, resolve dependencies for, and emit scripts and stylesheets. Two generations coexist: the classic WP_Dependencies handle system and WP_Script_Modules with ES modules and import maps.

name: global-styles-theme-json
purpose: A declarative styling system. theme.json describes settings (what the editor offers) and styles (what is applied), merged across four origins and compiled to CSS.

name: rewrite-and-permalinks
purpose: Two inverse operations: compile a permalink structure into regex rules mapping URLs to query variables, and generate URLs from objects. WordPress's router.

name: block-supports
purpose: Cross-cutting block features. A block declares supports in block.json and this module injects the resulting classes and inline styles at render time, so no block implements colour or spacing handling itself.

name: embeds-oembed
purpose: Turn a bare URL on its own line into rich embedded content, and expose WordPress's own posts as oEmbed providers.

name: interactivity-api
purpose: Declarative client-side interactivity driven by data-wp-* HTML attributes, with server-side pre-rendering of directives so the initial HTML is already correct.

name: rest-api
purpose: WordPress's HTTP API. A route registry, a dispatcher with a schema-driven validate/sanitize pipeline, and 49 controllers exposing core entities at /wp-json/.

name: xmlrpc
purpose: The legacy remote API: 78 methods across five protocol families, predating REST by a decade and still enabled by default.

name: ai-abilities-connectors
purpose: The newest subsystem: a registry of typed, permission-gated, schema-described abilities that AI agents can discover and invoke, plus a provider-agnostic AI client.

name: http-api
purpose: Make outbound HTTP requests portably, with a safe variant defending against Server-Side Request Forgery. Underlies updates, oEmbed discovery, feeds, the block directory and every plugin calling a remote service.

name: feeds
purpose: Publish content as RSS 2.0, RSS 0.92, RDF and Atom, and consume external feeds via SimplePie.

name: sitemaps
purpose: Generate XML sitemaps for search engines from a small provider-based architecture.

name: admin-application
purpose: The /wp-admin/ application: 95 screen files, 106 shared includes, 30 network screens, 10 per-user screens, plus the menu system, list tables and admin-ajax.

name: multisite
purpose: Run many sites from one installation, sharing users and a codebase while separating content.

name: deprecated-compat
purpose: Keep code written for WordPress 1.5 working on WordPress 7.2, and polyfill newer PHP functions so core can use modern syntax on PHP 7.4.

name: updates-and-upgrader
purpose: Check for, download, verify and install core, plugin, theme and translation updates, and migrate the database schema between versions.

name: site-health
purpose: Run diagnostic tests and surface configuration problems, with a debug-data collector for support.

name: filesystem-api
purpose: Write files portably, including on hosts where PHP cannot write directly and must go through FTP or SSH; plus Ed25519 verification of update packages.

name: internationalization
purpose: Translate strings, resolve the active locale, and switch locale mid-request.

name: performance-speculation-view-transitions
purpose: Modern browser-performance primitives: the Speculation Rules API for prefetch and prerender, plus View Transitions.

name: cron
purpose: Schedule deferred and recurring work. WordPress has no daemon; cron is a queue in an option, drained by piggybacking on incoming HTTP requests.
